final_candidates.title: Node credentials : Node-RED
final_candidates.product_feature: Separate runtime credential values and editor presence metadata
final_candidates.version_or_date: Live undated documentation read 2026-11-24; applicability of this edition to 3.1.3 is unknown
final_candidates.exact_section: Node credentials, line 28; Accessing credentials / Runtime use of credentials and Credentials within the Editor, lines 64–81
final_candidates.input_processing_observation: Directly read: node password values are unavailable in the editor; a boolean indicates their presence. Runtime node code can access credential values. The documented object is a node credential, not a global environment variable.
final_candidates.what_is_new_vs_baseline: The supplied baseline already reports the failure and a prior flow-level fix. This page adds an explicit editor/runtime representation boundary to inspect. Whether the author already knew this contract is unknown.
final_candidates.changed_choice: Proposed transfer: represent an untouched secret as presence and edit intent, retaining its server-held value. Treat deliberate replacement as a separate operation; do not infer a new secret from a displayed mask.
final_candidates.minimal_discriminating_input: PROPOSED T1, not executed: create global SECRET='s-A' (credential) and LABEL='old' (plaintext), with an Inject flow reading SECRET. Keep that flow unchanged while changing LABEL to 'new'; separately repeat with only an Inject-flow edit. Observe editor presence metadata, outgoing credential fields, stored value, and runtime result. Control: explicitly replace SECRET with 's-B'.
final_candidates.expected_output: Under the proposed preservation contract, either unrelated edit leaves SECRET='s-A', while the deliberate replacement yields 's-B'. A mask first appearing as secret data at the save boundary supports a serialization hypothesis; an unchanged saved secret with a masked runtime result points elsewhere.
conditions_supported: Official per-node documentation demonstrates that an editor can know a secret exists without possessing its bytes.
Transfer to global environment editing is a design inference, not a verified Node-RED API guarantee.
final_candidates.limitations: The global-variable implementation, actual requests, persistence, and runtime were not inspected. This source does not identify the defect or its repair.
final_candidates.counter_evidence: Per-node credential handling may differ from the global-environment path. The reported runtime output alone does not establish that storage was overwritten.
final_candidates.historical_availability: Unknown: no publication date, archived 2024 edition, or version-pinned implementation was read.

final_candidates.title: kv patch - Command | Vault | HashiCorp Developer
final_candidates.product_feature: KV v2 partial secret updates and alternative read-modify-write mode
final_candidates.version_or_date: Page displays Vault v2.x (latest); KV v2 engine; read 2026-11-24; publication date unknown
final_candidates.exact_section: kv patch, lines 267–290; Usage / Command options, lines 309–313
final_candidates.input_processing_observation: Directly read: KV patch preserves existing data while applying supplied changes. Full put requires existing values too. The CLI offers server PATCH and a client read-modify-write mode, exposing where the complete secret state is assembled.
final_candidates.what_is_new_vs_baseline: Adds an explicit partial-update versus complete-replacement choice for a secret-bearing collection. The supplied post lists a failing UI sequence but does not specify its save semantics. This is absent from that list; author familiarity is unknown.
final_candidates.changed_choice: Proposed transfer: inspect whether global-variable saving should merge only changed entries against server-held credentials, keyed by stable variable identity. A redacted editor snapshot cannot supply all original values for a complete replacement.
final_candidates.minimal_discriminating_input: PROPOSED T2, not executed: seed a save-boundary fixture with SECRET='s-A' and LABEL='old'. Submit an update containing only EXTRA='new', omitting SECRET. Compare with the current full editor payload. Then deliberately submit SECRET='s-B'. Record exactly whether omitted credentials survive and whether explicit replacements still take effect.
final_candidates.expected_output: For the proposed partial-update contract, the first update retains SECRET='s-A' and LABEL='old' and adds EXTRA; the deliberate update yields SECRET='s-B'. If omission loses SECRET, the tested boundary behaves as replacement or requires a different contract. If omission works but the full redacted payload fails, inspect serialization of unchanged secrets.
conditions_supported: Vault documents preservation under partial KV updates and the need for existing values when performing complete replacement.
The server-patch versus client-read-modify-write distinction makes the location of secret reconstruction explicit.
final_candidates.limitations: This is a mechanism analogy, not a recommendation to deploy Vault or evidence that Node-RED accepts PATCH. Node-RED's collection shape and stable identifiers are unknown.
final_candidates.counter_evidence: Documented functionality is KV v2-specific. A merge cannot repair a request that explicitly supplies the mask as a new secret; edit intent still needs correct encoding.
final_candidates.historical_availability: Unknown at 2024-01-03. The page's version selector reports no versions of this document before v1.16.x; an example's 2019 timestamp is not a publication or feature-introduction date.
